key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically sustained hexagonal ZrO interlayer that helps explain columnar oxide microstructures and may slow oxygen transport during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: Predicting oxide morphology, oxygen transport barriers, and local tensile stresses could improve assessments of zirconium corrosion and crack initiation.
method: Compute ZrOₓ thermochemistry, elasticity, and interface properties using DFT.
Use DFT-trained machine-learned molecular dynamics to supply additional material inputs.
Simulate oxide growth with a phase-field model coupling diffusion, heterogeneous nucleation, and strain-dependent phase stability.
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduce columnar oxide morphology and grain-size distributions observed in micrographs, as well as an undulating metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors or direct kinetic measurements confirming the proposed ZrO barrier's contribution to sub-parabolic corrosion.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
